pairs.difference: A beach ball: soft, even shading over the whole sphere. The darker side sits low on the lower right with a gentle gradient, and there is one soft cast shadow on the sand. The lens range is low (0.533, below real). B dock: the posts and lifebuoy have a clear lit top and darker side, and each post sits in a dark contact ring on the water. Light comes from the upper left, as on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the ball from the upper left so the right and bottom quarter turns clearly darker. Add a small, sharp white highlight near the upper left and a darker contact shadow where the ball touches the sand.

pairs.difference: B pocket watch: the gold case is lit almost evenly all the way round, with no real shadow side. The face is flat, and the cast shadow under it is faint and blurry. A ring box: the velvet box has a clear darker right side and inner walls, and the medal sits in a darker recess.
pairs.fix: Light the watch from the upper left so the right half of the gold rim drops into a deep shadow. Add a bright glint on the upper left of the rim and a soft, darker shadow under the case.

pairs.difference: A hatbox: the cylinder has one broad, smooth sheen down its middle and little core shadow on the right edge. The lid top is flat and evenly lit. Form contrast is 0.363, below real. B sneakers: there is a clear light side and shadow side on the soles and uppers, with a dark contact shadow to the left.
pairs.fix: Make the right third of the hatbox clearly darker, with a defined core shadow running down the drum. Make the lid's top face brighter than its side band, and darken the contact line at the base.

pairs.difference: A pearl bracelet: every bead has the same small, centered highlight and the same soft falloff. There is no side of the bracelet that is lit or in shadow, and only faint contact darkening on the cushion. Contrast and light bias are both very low (0.263 and 0.043). B map and magnifier: light falls clearly from one side, the lens throws a cast shadow, and the map folds alternate between lit and shaded.
pairs.fix: Light the bracelet from the upper left so the pearls on the lower right fall into shadow. Give each pearl a highlight on its upper left and a small dark contact shadow where it presses into the cushion.

pairs.difference: A cake stand: the porcelain plates and post are pale and evenly lit. The plates' undersides are barely darker than their tops, and the petit fours have almost no shadow side. Range and contrast are both below real. B fountain: the stone basins have dark undersides and inner walls, and the tiers cast clear shadows onto each other.
pairs.fix: Make the underside of each plate and the right side of the post clearly darker. Give each little cake a darker right side, and cast a firm shadow from the top plate onto the cakes below.

pairs.difference: B folding fan: the pleats alternate light and dark in a regular stripe pattern instead of following one light direction. The whole fan reads front-lit, with only a faint cast shadow on the background. A scarf: the fabric has a rounded light-to-shadow turn on the neck loop and the tails, with darker folds under the knot.
pairs.fix: Light the fan from the upper left. Make the pleats facing left bright and the pleats facing right darker, getting darker toward the right edge. Add a soft shadow under the fan on the background.

pairs.difference: A scroll: one strong side light makes the right end bright, and there is a glossy reflection on the table. The roll itself turns from light to shadow in a shallow, smooth way. Light bias is 0.924, above real. B DJ deck: lighting is balanced from the top left, the deck has clearly darker sides, and the headphones have a contact shadow.
pairs.fix: Turn the scroll's light down to a gentle upper-left key. Darken the underside of the roll into a clear core shadow and add a soft contact shadow where it rests on the table.

pairs.difference: B top hat: the crown has one broad, smooth sheen on the left and blends evenly into the dark right side. The brim underside has little bounce, and form contrast is lower (0.418). A graduation cap: the board has a lit flat top, a darker front edge with a crisp corner, and a deep shadow inside the crown.
pairs.fix: Put a narrow highlight on the hat's crown at the upper left. Add a darker core shadow down the right side of the crown, then a faint cool rim light at the edge. Cast a darker shadow from the brim onto the band.

pairs.difference: A trunk: the top is lit and the side planes are darker, but the shadow on the stone floor is heavy and spread out, and the lighting on the front face is gritty and uneven. B suitcase: it is lit from the front and backlit by the sunburst, with soft rim light on the corners and an even front face. Its range is slightly low. On this vector the call is unclear.
pairs.fix: Give the trunk smooth, clean light. Make the top bright, the front face a mid tone and the right side clearly darker, with soft bevels on the straps. Add a compact contact shadow at the base.

pairs.difference: B teacup: the glossy cup has broad, soft lighting with a weak shadow side. The saucer is evenly lit and has only a soft, diffuse shadow under it. Form contrast is 0.471, lower than A. A vending machine: there is a clear lit front and darker side panel, a crisp edge highlight, and a contact shadow at the feet.
pairs.fix: Light the cup from the upper left so its right side and the inside of the handle turn clearly darker. Add a small, sharp highlight on the rim and a darker contact shadow where the cup sits on the saucer.

pairs.difference: A folding fan: the pleats alternate light and dark as flat stripes, and there is no overall light-to-shadow turn across the fan. There is no cast shadow, and the background glow is centered. Contrast is 0.213 and light bias 0.09, both well below real. B parasol: the canopy is lit on the left and drops into a deep shadow on the right, each panel turns in a rounded way, and the frilled edge is shaded.
pairs.fix: Light the fan from the upper left, from bright on the left pleats to darker on the right pleats. Make the pleat folds crisp, with a dark crease line, and put a soft shadow under the fan on the background.

pairs.difference: B piano: it is lit flat from the front. The lid, front panels and legs are nearly the same value, and the side planes are barely darker. Light bias is 0.144, below real. A guitar: the spotlight logic is clear, with a lit body edge, a darker lower side and a contact shadow on the stage.
pairs.fix: Light the piano from the upper left so the right side panel and the underside of the keyboard shelf fall into a clear shadow. Make the top of the lid bright, and add a dark contact shadow under the legs and pedals.

pattern: The generated cards are lit flat from the front. Their light does not commit to a direction, so the shadow side stays shallow and parts that repeat (pearls, fan pleats, plate rims) all get the same centered shading. Folds alternate light and dark as stripes instead of following one light. Sheen is broad and soft, and cast and contact shadows are faint or missing. Real cards put a clear key light at the upper left with a darker core shadow on the right and firm contact darkening.
